title: Mental addition & subtraction
examples: Can you show me how to add 8 and 5 quickly?
What is a good trick for adding numbers close to ten?
Can you explain the compensation method with an example?

explain.say: You can add in your head. Some ways make it quicker.

items: Add ten, then take one away

explain.say: Add seven and six. Seven needs three more to make ten. Take three from the six. Three is left. Ten and three make thirteen.
Doubles are two of the same number. Six and six make twelve.
Near doubles are one away from a double. Eight plus nine is eight plus eight, and one more. That makes seventeen.
To add nine, add ten and take one away. Twelve plus ten is twenty-two. Take one away to make twenty-one.
To take away, you can count up. For twelve take away nine, count up from nine to twelve. That is three.

faq.a: It means finding the small number needed to reach the next ten. For example, if you have 8, you need 2 to make 10.
asks: How do I get to ten quickly?
What is the trick for making ten?

faq.q: When should I use near doubles?
faq.a: You use this when the two numbers you add are very close to being the same. It is faster than adding them straight away.
asks: What if the numbers are far apart?

faq.a: Compensation means making the numbers easier to work with first. You change them a little, and then you fix your answer.
asks: Can I use it for subtraction too?

faq.q: Do I have to use these tricks all the time?
faq.a: No, you can use any way you know. These are just quicker ways to work out a sum.
asks: Is there a right way to add?
When should I just count my fingers?

faq.q: Which trick is best for big numbers?
faq.a: For very large numbers, compensation by rounding to the nearest hundred can be very helpful. It keeps the calculation simple.
asks: Which trick is for big numbers?
Is there a trick for hundreds?

facts: Bridging ten helps you add numbers that are close to a multiple of ten.
Near doubles means adding two numbers that are almost equal.
Compensation involves rounding numbers to make addition easier.
These ways help you answer sums quickly in your head.

quiz.say: Make ten first. Tap the answer.
quiz.why: 9 needs 1 to make 10, and 6 is left from the 7. So 10 and 6 make 16.

wrong.0: Take 1 from the 7 to make 10, and that leaves 6 to add.
wrong.2: The 1 you gave to the 9 came from the 7, so only 6 is left to add.

quiz.say: Use a double to help. Tap the answer.
quiz.why: 6 + 6 = 12. 7 is one more than 6, so the answer is 13.

wrong.0: 7 + 7 = 14 is one too many, because 6 is one less than 7.
wrong.1: 6 + 6 = 12, and you need one more for the 7.

quiz.say: Add ten, then take one away. Tap the answer.

wrong.1: 21 is 11 + 10, so take one away for the 9.
wrong.2: From 21, take away just 1, and you get 20.
